question: Does inference-time reasoning improve action selection when the same supplied constraint information is available?
role: Constraint-aware prompting controls on existing P1 checkpoints; P1 and P2 are archived baselines

methods.name: Zero-shot CoT
methods.procedure: Generate reasoning using the original cot_trigger_no=1, then extract a final answer in a second generation

methods.name: Plan-and-Solve
methods.procedure: Use original basic PS prompt_201 for planning and solving, following the official answer-extraction procedure; no PS+ substitutions or self-consistency

checkpoints: Reuse existing P1 final LoRA checkpoints for all three task families and seeds
model_input: Original CoC with the frozen P1 natural-language rule
forbidden_model_input: Oracle metadata beyond the supplied P1 text
failure_accounting: Invalid outputs remain in the denominator; report their frequency separately and do not invent an action label or an admissibility verdict
budget_accounting: Original code defaults give unequal reasoning token caps; report actual cost and do not claim equal inference budgets
interpretation_limits: Prompting-procedure transfer to our Qwen VLM, not original GPT-model benchmark reproduction
P1 and its prompting controls use identical checkpoints, images and rule-bearing text; only inference instructions/extraction change
P2 expresses the same supplied task rules with CNL and uses its own matched-budget archived checkpoint; this does not isolate verification causally
Native reasoning caps remain 128 and 256; actual token usage and synchronized batch generation time are reported
These label-trained checkpoints may emit option labels without multistep reasoning; raw outputs are retained
Existing synthetic test rows and seeds are reused; no new training, independent road scenes, human labels or original DriveLM/DriveVLM execution
reporting_gate: Only report scored results after all three families and seeds finish; input and adapter hashes are frozen before inference
